acceptance_criteria.criterion: The cutoff gates on the authoritative PR number derived from the directory a record was found under, never on a self-declared field inside the record; a record whose own 'pr' disagrees with its directory is rejected naming both values
reviews/schema.json is enforced -- required fields, declared types with bool excluded from integer, enums, and the reviewed_commit hex pattern -- where previously nothing loaded it at all
A reviewer identity parses as <role>-<model>-<session-token>-<date> from the right, so real identifiers containing hyphens are expressible without degrading them to satisfy the validator

An accidental self-review is caught by comparing both ids as sets of hyphen-delimited segments, verified against the ten real records: PRs 15, 16 and 17 flagged on a genuinely shared token, PRs 7 through 13 and 18 clean
A record must declare whether the reviewer was dispatched by the author, and a true declaration is ANNOUNCED in the gate's output rather than passing silently as though it were independence
A non-string reviewed_commit no longer crashes the script with an uncaught TypeError, verified even when schema validation is bypassed entirely

tokens.source: transcript message.usage summed across this session's usage-bearing assistant records. Covers the WHOLE session across PRs 12-19, not this deliverable alone, and EXCLUDES all subagent spend -- this PR alone ran an implementer and a reviewer through three rounds each, none of it in this transcript. A floor, not a total.

unproven: THIS RECORD'S OWN checked_by IS NOT INDEPENDENT. reviews/19/ declares reviewer_was_dispatched_by_author: true -- the reviewer is a subagent of the author's session, and said so itself after twice refusing to claim otherwise. The gate announced it in four NOTICE lines, one per commit touching a shared path -- counted from the captured output in this record's own commands, not from memory. This is the first record in the repo to state this; nine of the ten before it were produced the same way and said nothing.

The declaration cannot be verified. A dishonest actor writes false as easily as inventing a distinct id was before. It raises the cost of an accident and creates a paper trail; it is not a security control and is not built as one.

A shared token shorter than 8 characters goes undetected. Not hypothetical: reviews/schema.json accepts a 7-character git short sha as a legitimate identifier, and a UUID's later groups are 4 characters. No floor value closes this without reopening the false positives the floor exists to prevent. Recorded beside the constant and in reviews/README.md.

The hand-rolled schema validator still ignores minLength, minimum, maximum, items, nested properties and additionalProperties. None is currently exploitable against reviews/schema.json -- the reviewer checked each -- but it is a real generic gap.

Command tails and sha256 values are SANITIZED by a per-session throwaway script rather than committed code. Still the first open blocker in docs/maintainers/proof-of-completion-plan.md, and still why no historical digest here is independently reproducible.
The env-leak history scan is the AUTHOR's result; the reviewer holds no repository secret and was told not to guess private-name values. CI's run is the only independent check.
The token figures are a FLOOR excluding all subagent spend, produced by an unreviewed measuring script.
All CI reasoning in the review is static analysis of the workflow file. No reviewer observed a live Actions run of these changes.
This record was written by the author of the work it proves.
